550005: Holo-magnetics are specialty pigments that degrade over time due to the solvents in nail polish base (not to be confused with regular holos). Because of this, I offer these partially mixed only. The dry pigment should remain effective for 10+ years. Dakini is a holo-magnetic made sheer so as to preserve the holoiest holo. It is inspired by the Tibetan and Vajrayana Buddhist interpretations of dakini, who are the ethereal, enigmatic female embodiments of enlightenment. The Tibetan word for dakini is khandro, which means sky-goer or space-dancer. Swatch stick photos are without top coat and from left right feature Dakini, Kuzuryū, Hōō, and Qilin. Last videos are of one coat of Dakini glass bead next to velvet under flash. For the strongest holographic effect I suggest using the glass bead technique. Instructions for mixing: I will provide the polish base, a small container of pigment, and a 10mg measuring spoon so that you can mix in a separate dish per manicure. If you don’t have a mixing dish already I will soon have some available under “Nail Care.” For 2 generous coats on swatch wheel nails the ratios work out like this: 25 drops of polish, 1 rounded spoon Dakini 25 drops of polish, 2 rounded spoons Kuzuryū, Hōō, and Qilin These pigments are so beautiful and are absolutely worth the couple extra steps in my opinion. I hope you enjoy them as much as I do! The mix-as-you-go method is demonstrated in the first two videos, and the one for Qilin includes audio commentary and clean-up footage. Written instructions are below. Mix-as-you-go Method: These instructions are for one hand with short to medium length nails. For two hands or long nails, multiply everything by two or more as needed. 1. Gather your materials: you will need the polish base, dry pigment, tiny spoon, a dropper (optional), a mixing dish, and acetone and a paper towel for cleanup. Suitable materials for mixing dishes include glass, ceramic, stainless steel, and disposable cups. 2. Prep your nails as you normally would. 3. Apply base coat. 4. Using the nail polish brush or dropper, drop 25 medium-to-large drops of base into your dish, OR use the dropper to measure out a tiny bit over .5ml (the precise measurement is .6ml). Don’t worry, it doesn’t have to be exact! 5. If using Dakini, take your tiny spoon, scoop up one spoon of holo, and add to the base. If using Kuzuryū, Hōō, or Qilin, scoop up two spoons of holo, and add to the base. 6. Mix it up using the nail polish brush, or if you desire, a separate brush or mixing tool. 7. Apply to nails and magnetize as desired, making sure to re-magnetize after top coat. 8. Pour a small amount of acetone into the dish. 9. Wipe the brush off with a tissue or paper towel and swish in acetone to remove polish residue, wipe again, and place back in the bottle. You can also use the acetone to rinse out the glass part of the dropper. 10. Wipe the dish to clean for later use. This step may have to wait until your nails are dry so as not to disturb your manicure, or you can use the cotton ball method as shown in the video for Qilin. Done! Enjoy the rainbows🥳 Part of the Celestial Harmony collection. 15ml Swatched by: reecebutglossy sammi.mani Demonstration videos by lacquer.and.light Me (Gel-X tips)

550030: Opossum is an “opossum nose pink” shimmer that glows in the dark like the full moon. This polish is inspired by the often misunderstood marsupial, the opossum. ”They’re often believed to be stupid, dirty creatures, but the truth is just the opposite – possums are smarter, cleaner, and more beneficial to humans than many of their wild neighbors. While they’re not the cutest creatures [I beg to differ], they should be a welcome addition to your backyards. Unlike other mammals that carry ticks, and potentially spread Lyme Disease, possums gobble up more than 90 percent of the ticks they encounter. Since they constantly self-groom with their tongues and paws, they’re one of the cleanest critters you’ll come across. And while they’re not totally immune to rabies, they rarely carry it. As a marsupial, possums have a lower body temperature than most other mammals, so their bodies don’t provide a suitable environment for the virus. So when you come across an opossum, don’t fear – just give it a little room to wander away so it can continue being a good, helpful neighbor.” https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/opossums.htm Part of the Hidden Gems collection. 15ml Swatched by: deepika5 sammi.mani sailormanimoon marainalacquer_ leanaswatches Me (GelX tips)
